items.title: Round 2 — Cards and Conversations
items.content: GM ONLY — Hand out the Round 2 cards together and give Dakota her deep-red envelope. Dakota has the compact; Scooter will ask her about it and borrow it to show Beverly. These represent earlier fictional events; no real sampling or dosing takes place. Help guests find the people named on their cards and allow time for conversation. Plain paper is available if somebody prefers to send a personal note. You may hand out evidence, but the guests discuss what it means. There is no collection meeting, reporting duty or delivery check.

items.title: Two Kinds of Paperwork
items.content:
Vale sold your masters and left you carrying the debt, but you never knew which of the paperwork behind it was honest.

You have heard that Sid Scrape faked signatures for Vale in the old days. If yours was one of them, your debt might not be real. Ask Sid which contracts he forged and which he did not.

items.title: Old Reunion Stories
items.content:
You were a punk legend and are now a dodgy pub landlord. Vale left you owing crushing money on a failed punk reunion, and you are desperate that nothing more surfaces. You want fear, not answers.

Find Robbie Rayne, the former boy-band heartthrob, Rex 'Razor' Steele and Roxy Riot. Vale is planning a reunion tour for them; tell them how yours ended. A bad bargain is easier to admit when somebody else has one too.

items.title: The Masters He Sold
items.content:
Vale sold your recording masters and left you owing money on a failed punk reunion. You were afraid of what else he might release. Being angry about that hardly makes you unique among his former stars.

Compare your experience with Robbie Rayne. Ask what Vale wanted from the tour he announced.

items.title: What You Saw in the Lobby
items.content:
You watched Robbie in the lobby from 19:28 until the 19:30 alarm. He stayed there signing and talking and did not return to the main room. You cannot give that account for everybody in the passage. You never heard Robbie raise his voice to Vale about the tour.

Tell Sabrina Sinclair what you saw. You owe Vale money you will never repay, and the truth about where somebody else stood is all you have worth trading.

items.title: The Signatures You Supplied
items.content:
You forged signatures on music contracts for Vale's company. He kept the proof, so you did what he wanted. You did not forge Veronica's contract.

People say Ricky Blaze forged Vale's signature on a loan. Ask Ricky what Vale did with it. Did Vale use him the same way he used you?

items.title: The Old Record Business
items.content:
You are an old-school punk. You are still angry, and you trust nobody. You forged signatures on music contracts for Vale's company, and he kept the proof. You are terrified it will come out.

Find Penny Page, the script editor, and Wanda Wires, the lighting technician, and talk about paperwork: whose name goes on it, and who signs it. You know more about that than you will admit.

items.title: What You Did Not Forge
items.content:
You forged some music-contract signatures for Vale. That was wrong, and it was you. But you did not forge Veronica's contract. You did not forge Johnny's either: his debt is real. Nobody can blame every paper in Vale's archive on you.

Sabrina Sinclair is writing Vale's big story. Ask her what title he gave it, and when it was meant to be printed.

items.title: A Signature of Her Own
items.content:
You say you were in the passage during the music, but nobody watched you the whole time.

You faked plenty of signatures for Vale. People say he made Wanda Wires sign off a rehearsal before it was finished, then kept the paper over her. Ask Wanda what that was like. Is signing your own name under pressure any better than faking someone else's?

items.title: What Is VV-1?
items.content:
You were away from the private drink during the toast, though nobody watched you throughout.

Everyone is talking about VV-1, and Barry Byte seems to have a copy. Ask him what this VV-1 everyone is talking about actually is. You want to know whether it holds the secret you have been defending.

items.title: An Uncomfortable Curiosity
items.content:
You are a Welsh colliery worker and union organiser, recently sacked, and not afraid to say what you think. Vale bribed you to break the strike, and you are angry with yourself for taking it. You suspect he also gathered proof of your overly friendly Soviet trade contacts, and passed it to people here with intelligence connections.

Find Tina 'Tank' Thatcher, a fellow union activist, Agent 'Rosemary' and Sir Giles Houghton. Is their interest in you professional or merely rude?

items.title: The Payment He Could Expose
items.content:
Vale bribed you to break the strike. You fear he also kept proof of your overly friendly Soviet trade contacts.

If that proof exists, it is on tape somewhere, and Barry Byte, the ByteCorp salesman, boasts that he supplied Vale's tapes. Ask him what copies exist, and whether anything about you could have survived.

items.title: A Fear Without a File
items.content:
You fear exposure of your strike money and Soviet contacts, but do not know that either was in the recording meant for the toast.

You know what it is to be paid and not ask why. DJ Spinny T took an envelope tonight and did as it told him. Ask him what he was paid to do, and whether he ever learned who wanted it.

items.title: A Disturbed Cover
items.content:
You are an heiress and a wild child, and your feelings show on your face. Vale caught you stealing from him and planned to ruin you. You noticed the cover and seal on Vale's separate dish had been disturbed after it was marked ready, and had it withdrawn.

Find Dr. Beverly Steele, the Harley Street surgeon, Dakota Steele, the private eye, and Inspector Donna Reed, and talk about how the evening is being run. You have views on the service.

items.title: The Dish You Stopped
items.content:
The dish labelled for Vale never reached him. Its cover was loose and its seal disturbed, so you had staff withdraw it and keep it for checking.

You also saw him pour from his private decanter. He already seemed unusually sharp before that final drink, though you did not see when that began.

Ask Dr. Beverly Steele, the Harley Street doctor, what his earlier manner could tell you about the collapse.

items.title: An Explanation Overdue
items.content:
You stopped Vale's separate dish because its cover and seal had been disturbed. It never reached him. You then stayed at the service hatch with Beverly through the music and the alarm.

Find Dr. Beverly Steele, the Harley Street doctor, and ask directly whether she put anything in that dish.

items.title: At the Service Hatch
items.content:
After the service check, you remained at the hatch with Beverly and the supervisor from 19:28:45 until the 19:30 alarm. You could see the main room, but could not reach the private decanter from there. You did not touch it.

Ask Lady Helena de Brissac what she saw of the covered dish being taken back; she may have seen another part of its journey.

items.title: The Cost of Protection
items.content:
You are a Soviet defector and a ballerina, elegant and controlled. Years ago you were Vale's mistress. He promised to protect your reputation and your career, and once promised you a share of his estate: enough, he said, that you would never dance for money again.

Find Wendy Woke, the Marxist poet, Lady Helena de Brissac and Cassette Carl, and talk about what protection costs. You grew up where Wendy's views were compulsory.

items.title: Behind a Composed Face
items.content:
A dead man's promise of money is exactly what people whisper about, and Chuck Chambers has made a living selling what people say in Vale's green room.

Ask Chuck Chambers what the green room says about you and Vale's money, and whether your name has been sold with the rest.

items.title: What He Promised
items.content:
Vale promised to protect your reputation and career after your relationship, and promised you part of his estate. You never saw it in writing. Only his brother, Peter Vale, who has arrived after the collapse, will know what it is worth now.

Ask Peter Vale where he was before arriving, and whether he expects to inherit a lot.

items.title: A Promise and a Written Right
items.content:
Peter Vale seemed very interested in what Vale promised you. A brother who asks what you were promised is counting what is left.

Ask Peter Vale, Vincent's brother, what he read about Vincent's claim on Veronica's future fees, and what that leaves in the estate. If Vincent's death has made his own family poorer, the money that matters is somebody else's.

items.title: Surviving a Long Evening
items.content:
You are an aerobics instructor and self-help guru, all energy and positivity. You coached Vale's mistresses for extra cash, Roxie Runway among them, and he could use that against you and against them. You read people through their bodies: tension, stress, careful movement.

Find Roxie Runway, the supermodel, Ronnie Reels, the independent filmmaker, and Marianne Moonbeam, the alternative healer. Compare ways of keeping people going, and watch Ronnie Reels' hands while he talks.

items.title: The Familiar Signs
items.content:
You noticed Ronnie Reels' quick speech and restless hands. Vale also seemed sharp and restless before his final drink. You can describe those signs, but your work as an aerobics instructor does not tell you which drug or dose caused them.

Ask Ronnie Reels, the filmmaker, about the support he received from Beverly.

items.title: What a Conversation Reveals
items.content:
You saw restless behaviour in Ronnie Reels and Vale, not a compact being opened or wine being interfered with. It is easy to sound knowledgeable about somebody's nerves and still know very little about what happened.

Ask Marianne Moonbeam what she saw when Beverly spoke with Ronnie Reels.

items.title: Why He Kept Quiet
items.content:
You saw the same signs in Vale and in Ronnie Reels, hours apart, and you were right about both: something was keeping them running. Naming it is a doctor's job, not yours, but noticing it was never nothing.

Ask Ronnie Reels, the filmmaker, why he kept what he saw to himself until now. You suspect you already know part of the answer.

items.title: Respectable Business
items.content:
You bootleg mixtapes, and Vale was your biggest buyer: copied rehearsals, duplicates, insurance copies. Tonight you are listening for who sounds frightened enough to pay for silence. You would also like to look less like a bootlegger and more like a businessman, and a businessman needs respectable friends.

Find Lady Helena de Brissac, Sasha Smirnoff and Wendy Woke. Ask Helena how someone in her position keeps a public reputation spotless.

items.title: An Old Title?
items.content:
You sold Vale copied band rehearsals and performances without permission, and the tapes were full of juicy gossip. You told yourself he wanted them for his archive; you always suspected they were leverage.

Lady Helena de Brissac seems a bit above her station. Grill her, charmingly, on how her family came by the title, and whether it is an old one.

items.title: A Juicy Rumour
items.content:
Your stock was copied rehearsals and performances. Now there is a rumour of a juicy BBC recording, the one Vale meant to play tonight, and you would dearly love to get hold of it.

Sabrina Sinclair is writing Vale's story about it. Ask her whether she ever heard the recording, or only his word for it.

items.title: The Price of a Recording
items.content:
You made money selling recordings to Vale, then watched him make money from people's fear of them.

Drop Wendy Woke a hint about what you sold your best customer, and see how she takes it. Then ask why she attacked Vale's control in her poem.

items.title: The Price of Silence
items.content:
You paid Vale to keep your name out of recordings that could damage your reputation and jewellery business. You never trusted him to keep his word. Buying silence was easier than feeling safe.

Tell Angie Vixen what that bargain felt like and ask what Vale did to her career.

items.title: A Polished Reputation
items.content:
You are a jewellery mogul, polished and persuasive. You paid Vale to keep your name out of any damaging recordings, and your brand depends on nothing surfacing tonight. Look as though you have never worried about anything more serious than a necklace clasp.

Find Miss Cherry Bomb, the cosmetics queen, Graham Greenwell, the pharmaceutical entrepreneur, and Polly Premium, the retired insurance assessor. Compare notes on building a brand, and ask Polly what a guarantee really covers.

items.title: Behind the Brand
items.content:
You paid Vale to keep damaging material quiet, and even with him gone you do not feel safe. You know a polished sales pitch covering private anxiety when you see one, and Marianne Moonbeam has the most otherworldly pitch in the room.

Ask Marianne Moonbeam to gaze into the auras here tonight and say whether any of it threatens you.

items.title: The Payment You Recognised
items.content:
Before the music cue, waiting for your wrap at the cloakroom, you saw Veronica slip a deep-red envelope into Dakota's open coat pocket. Dakota was facing the attendant. You saw Veronica clearly, but not what was inside the envelope.

You kept quiet because questions about other people's payments might lead back to yours. Find Dakota Steele, the private investigator, now. Tell her who left it and ask what the envelope contained.

items.title: A Familiar Face
items.content:
You built a fitness empire on VHS: the strength, the control, the woman who has it all together. The one thing you chose freely is hidden: you and Frankie Faith are secretly married. Vale filmed you both in the garden, and that footage could undo everything you have each built.

Find Frankie Faith and Crystal DeVille, the showbiz agent. Greet Frankie openly enough to look natural, then talk about keeping a public image under control.

items.title: Our Story, At Last
items.content:
You and Frankie stayed in the conservatory from before the music until after the collapse. He is your husband. You kept that private to protect your fitness empire and his ministry, but secrecy now risks making you look involved in something much worse.

Tell Polly Premium about the marriage and where you were. Let her hear a real explanation for the greeting she noticed.

items.title: The Image You Protect
items.content:
Frankie is your husband. You greeted him before slipping away together to discuss whether to acknowledge the marriage. Vale's film could damage the fitness image you built. For now, you are keeping the marriage, and where the two of you went, private.

Miss Cherry Bomb's business is an image too. Ask her what Vale could undo about her public image.

items.title: Someone Who Understands
items.content:
You stayed with Frankie in the conservatory from before the music until after the collapse. Naming him would expose the marriage you have kept secret, and you are not ready yet.

Vale filmed you both in the garden, and Lucien Luxe goes pale whenever anyone mentions Vale's cameras. Ask Lucien what Vale threatened to reveal about him.

items.title: Two Broken Things
items.content:
You had a sharp word with Vincent in a corridor before any of it. Then you smashed your champagne glass around 19:20 and broke a microphone at about 19:21, both before the toast music. From about 19:27 you were below the stage guardrail with the isolated ignition cable.

Ask Larry Loveboat what he noticed backstage. You would rather be accused of your actual temper than every crash in the building.

items.title: Beyond Your Own Outburst
items.content:
You were below the guardrail through the cue and alarm. You had already broken a glass and microphone earlier; anger does not give you a useful account of everybody else's movements.

Ask Cassie Chase where she stayed after the dish was withdrawn and who was with her. You want to understand another person's part in the evening for a change.

items.title: Below the Guardrail
items.content:
You were below the guardrail from about 19:27 through the music and alarm, dealing with the isolated ignition cable. You saw Larry pass, then return and stay. That does not mean he watched the whole interval.

Ask Larry Loveboat exactly when he saw you. You want his real account, even if it is less complete than you would like.

items.title: A Duet Under Strain
items.content:
You are a fading heavy-metal star, once king of the charts, now better known for temper and tequila. Your pyrotechnic performance was sabotaged before it began, and you have already had a tense word with Vincent. Now he is putting you and Roxy Riot on the Take Watt reunion tour as the support act. Support. For a boy band. Warming up a hall of screaming fans for Robbie Rayne. Really?

Find Roxy Riot, Robbie Rayne and Johnny 'Jet' Maxwell, and talk about the tour and tonight's duet.

items.title: The Private Life Behind the Image
items.content:
You are afraid of an intimate recording being turned into a public judgement. Vale knew precisely how to use that fear. You are not the only person whose carefully managed image hides a private relationship.

Ask Frankie Faith what Vale could expose about him. His answer may explain why a man so sure of his public message is reluctant to speak.

items.title: What a Glimpse Can Tell
items.content:
Vale's film of your affair was taken without consent; you know how easily an image can be made to tell somebody else's story.

Crystal DeVille has been telling people she saw a hand at the decanter from the balcony, and a glimpse like that can hang somebody. Ask her what she actually saw.

items.title: Managing an Unwanted Image
items.content:
You are a supermodel, glamorous and guarded. You had an affair with Vale, and he filmed it without your consent. The affair was yours; the recording was taken, and that is the part that stays with you.

Find Tina Tanktop, the aerobics guru, Ronnie Reels and Marianne Moonbeam, and talk about staying camera-ready through a long evening. Keep your composure.

items.title: A Camera Without Permission
items.content:
Vale kept footage of your affair, filmed without consent. That explains your fear of what he might reveal. You noticed his restless manner before the toast, but do not know what caused it.

Ask Tina Tanktop, the aerobics instructor, what she saw in his behaviour before the final drink. You want to know whether her observation matches yours.

items.title: The People Behind the Argument
items.content:
You criticised Vale's ownership and control in a poem, and he reacted sharply. You dislike the power he exercised over other people's work; you do not need a private scandal to explain your hostility.

Bring on the revolution! But first, find out who fed the machine: everyone knows Vale was Cassette Carl's best customer. Ask Carl what he sold Vale.

items.title: What Protection Costs
items.content:
You are a Marxist poet who sees hidden power structures everywhere. Vale stands for everything you despise: fame built on exploitation, money made by manipulation, power used to silence. Your poem attacking his control of other people's work drew a sharp reaction from him.

Find Sasha Smirnoff, the defector ballerina, Lady Helena de Brissac and Cassette Carl. Ask what Vale's protection and respectability cost them, before offering your opinion of men who control other people's careers.

items.title: The Price of Control
items.content:
You criticised Vale in a poem. Now his brother, Peter Vale, has been reading his private papers.

Ask Peter Vale, Vincent's brother, what Veronica's contract said: how much of her earnings could Vale take, and does that stop now he is dead?

items.title: A Bargain Under Pressure
items.content:
You do not mourn Vale's power, but the killing is a different matter. You want to understand the bargains people made when they felt they had no choice.

Ricky Blaze let slip that Vale held a forged signature over him. Ask Ricky what forging it left him afraid of, and let him explain the loan before you judge the man who held it over him.

items.title: What You Chose to Do
items.content:
You got into Vale's archive without permission and saw the VV-1 entry, not every private file. You were quietly working with GCHQ, but breaking in was your own choice. Admitting how you got in means admitting who you work for.

Nev once worked in intelligence too. Tell 'Nev' Neville how you got in, and ask why his past makes Vale's archive so frightening.

items.title: Talking Shop
items.content:
You are a hacker for hire with an official connection you keep quiet. You were asked to watch Vale's systems for sensitive leaks, but your access to his network was personal, and what you found there was not state business, just private leverage. Keep your knowledge technical, casual and deniable.

Find Colin Cable, the network engineer, and 'Nev' Neville, and talk shop about Vale's system. You would like to know how freely they talk about it.

items.title: The Entry You Found
items.content:
You entered Vale's archive without permission. You saw a release entry scheduled after the toast, but its contents and subject were hidden from view. Getting inside did not mean reading everything.

Ask Colin Cable how somebody could enter without leaving a reliable record. His answer may tell you how exposed your own visit was.

items.title: A Reference Without Contents
items.content:
You saw a recording labelled VV-1 scheduled for release after the toast. Its contents were hidden from you, and it would only play once somebody gave the play command.

Barry Byte sold Vale his tapes and kept copies. Ask him what his older copy contains, and whether its label matches the entry you saw.

items.title: Professional Caution
items.content:
You are a senior government man who keeps secrets for a living. You are here to find out whether Vale got hold of any government material. You never tell a lie, but you never say much either.

You know Agent 'Rosemary' from Whitehall, and nobody told you she would be here. Find her, Tina 'Tank' Thatcher and Ronnie Redhand, and chat about the evening, quietly. Hush-hush, naturally.

items.title: The Risk You Were Sent to Assess
items.content:
You were sent to check whether Vale had got hold of government secrets. You have no suspect, and no sign of any secret. If anything leaked, it was probably gossip.

Ask Chuck Chambers what he did with the gossip from Vale's green room.

items.title: A Concrete Observation
items.content:
Whatever happened tonight, it was not a government matter. But you did notice some odd behaviour: just before the toast, the music and stage lights rose together, as if on a signal, and Leo Lights was at the board.

Ask Leo Lights who asked him to arrange that cue.

items.title: A Former Identity
items.content:
You hear that somebody here once used another name. That could be about their past, not about tonight.

Ask Tina 'Tank' Thatcher, the Yorkshire activist, whether she once worked under another name, and whether she was sent here on a mission.

items.title: Beside the Sofa
items.content:
You photographed the ordinary champagne service, separate from Vale's private wine. Nikki found a passport under the sofa cushion while helping you retrieve a dropped envelope of photographs; your photographs do not show how it got there. The times check out, so take a pack of your prints to every table and leave it with them.

Ask Fiona Fringe what she noticed about the gown she designed, after the toast.
