items.title: Veronica Vane
items.description: Once adored by millions, Veronica has returned to the screen with perfect hair, immaculate glamour and rather more at stake than she cares to admit.

items.title: Lola Lasalle
items.description: A disciplined celebrity trainer who turned workouts into a home-video phenomenon and knows how to keep smiling under pressure.

items.title: Lucien Luxe
items.description: A stylish New Romantic pop star with an eye for drama, an immaculate public image and a talent for making an entrance.

items.title: Angie Vixen
items.description: The dramatic face of cult horror: expressive, theatrical and never afraid to turn a tense moment into a scene worth watching.

items.title: Glenda Gold
items.description: Polished, persuasive and dazzlingly well connected. Glenda built an empire from precious stones and treats reputation as her most valuable asset.

items.title: Graham Greenwell
items.description: A polished businessman developing a fashionable herbal remedy with Dr. Beverly Steele. He sees markets, packaging and opportunity everywhere.

items.title: Miss Cherry Bomb
items.description: A beauty-industry entrepreneur selling confidence in glamorous packaging, with the poise of someone who knows exactly how an image is constructed.

items.title: Roxy Riot
items.description: Vale Meridian's former voice of rebellion, now colder, darker and more theatrical. Roxy can still make a room feel like a live stage.

items.title: Tina Tanktop
items.description: A relentlessly upbeat fitness celebrity whose VHS empire combines Lycra, positive thinking and the promise of a completely new you.

items.title: Ronnie Reels
items.description: A driven director with a visual memory, relentless deadlines and a habit of observing the details outside the centre of the frame.

items.title: Marianne Moonbeam
items.description: A free-spirited healer, winemaker and believer in energies that the rest of the room may be too cynical to understand.

items.title: Peter Packard
items.description: An early backer of the digital future who understands that information, timing and confidence can be worth more than the hardware itself.

items.title: Tommy Tech
items.description: A Brummie microchip obsessive who sees the world as connected systems, fragile circuits and problems waiting to be debugged.

items.title: Roxie Runway
items.description: Runway glamour with a carefully guarded private life. Roxie understands that appearances are valuable and secrets even more so.

items.title: Crystal DeVille
items.description: A polished and ruthless career-maker who has spent decades deciding who gets access to fame and who is left waiting outside.

items.title: Frankie Faith
items.description: Immaculate, reassuring and permanently camera-ready. Frankie projects moral authority with all the polish of a prime-time broadcast.

items.title: Robbie Rayne
items.description: Once the smiling face of Take Watt, Robbie is now a guarded solo artist trying to keep the reunion atmosphere professionally cheerful.

items.title: Sid Scrape
items.description: Still angry, still confrontational and deeply suspicious of polished celebrities. Sid wears distrust as naturally as a battered leather jacket.

items.title: Johnny 'Jet' Maxwell
items.description: An ex-punk frontman now running a questionable pub, still carrying the swagger, grudges and survival instincts of the old scene.

items.title: Sabrina Sinclair
items.description: A sharp reporter from the News of the Screws, equipped with a notebook, a nose for fear and no intention of leaving without a headline.

items.title: Scooter
items.description: Quick, capable and easily overlooked. Scooter moves through crowded rooms delivering packages and hearing far more than people realise.

items.title: Sasha Smirnoff
items.description: Elegant, poised and rigorously controlled. Sasha carries herself with the discipline of someone who has crossed borders and survived powerful patrons.

items.title: Rex 'Razor' Steele
items.description: A pyrotechnic rock veteran with a reputation for spectacular performances, damaged dressing rooms and very loud opinions.

items.title: Penny Page
items.description: A sharp-witted Vale Meridian script editor who supplies the polished words, spots every missing credit and is ready for recognition.

items.title: Larry Loveboat
items.description: A velvet-voiced entertainer who treats every conversation as an intimate cabaret and every entrance as the start of a new number.

items.title: Cassie Chase
items.description: Money, glamour and a famously short fuse. Cassie wears her feelings openly, but she is far sharper than her reputation suggests.

items.title: Dr. Beverly Steele
items.description: Authoritative, expensive and accustomed to being the most knowledgeable person in the room, Beverly arrives with professional confidence and a discreet medical bag.

items.title: Vincent Vale
items.description: Vincent is the charismatic founder of Vale Meridian Studios.

items.title: Peter Vale
items.description: After his dramatic demise, his suave and calculating twin Peter arrives to take his place in the spotlight.
items.cue: Keep private until the Round 1 role change

items.title: Agent 'Rosemary'
items.description: A composed visitor from Cheltenham with excellent observational skills, a talent for blending in and a surprisingly professional interest in surveillance.

items.title: Chuck Chambers
items.description: Loud, charismatic and professionally fascinated by confrontation. Chuck can turn the smallest rumour into an hour of television.

items.title: Nikki Neon
items.description: A bright, ambitious backing singer with sharp instincts, stage discipline and every intention of being remembered after the final chorus.

items.title: Vance Vellum
items.description: Charming, perceptive and rarely without a Polaroid. Vance knows that an unguarded moment makes a much better story than a posed portrait.

items.title: Sir Giles Houghton
items.description: A controlled senior figure accustomed to handling sensitive matters quietly, carefully and well away from public scrutiny.

items.title: Tina 'Tank' Thatcher
items.description: Tough, outspoken and politically charged, with a formidable understanding of power, information and the people who try to control both.

items.title: Barry Byte
items.description: A slick evangelist for the computer age who always has a brochure, a backup and another deal ready to close.

items.title: Mandy Modem
items.description: Fast, elusive and fluent in machines most guests barely understand. Mandy treats locked systems as invitations rather than obstacles.

items.title: Fiona Fringe
items.description: An architect of the unmistakable 1980s silhouette. Fiona reads clothes like evidence and spots alterations that nobody else would notice.

items.title: Colin Cable
items.description: Quiet and precise, Colin understands how information moves through a system and how much people reveal when they think nobody is listening.

items.title: 'Nev' Neville
items.description: An intelligent but uneasy systems specialist who sees too many connections, trusts almost nobody and handles every conversation with care.

items.title: Ronnie Redhand
items.description: A formidable Welsh woman, recently sacked and in no mood to be diplomatic. Ronnie brings blunt questions, union conviction and a deep distrust of media power.

items.title: Family Solicitor
items.description: Well-meaning, slightly pompous and not quite as competent as he believes. The family solicitor keeps proceedings official, or at least official-looking.

items.title: DJ Spinny T
items.description: A former pirate broadcaster who can control the mood of a room with impeccable timing, the right record and a well-placed distraction.

items.title: Inspector Donna Reed
items.description: An off-duty detective who never truly clocks off. Calm, procedural and difficult to distract once the evening takes a suspicious turn.

items.title: Dakota Steele
items.description: Discreet, observant and methodical. Dakota notices movements, objects and timings that pass everyone else by.

items.title: Leo Lights
items.description: A lighting professional with an eye on the next rung of the ladder. Leo understands cues, power and what should happen when a switch is thrown.

items.title: Brenda Blip
items.description: Energetic, connected and always listening. Brenda knows how to read a room through a pair of headphones and recognise a scoop when she hears one.

items.title: Polly Premium
items.description: A retired insurance claims assessor with a sharp eye for small print, a flawless filing system and a polite air of never having been surprised.

items.title: Ricky Blaze
items.description: A former screen daredevil who swapped film sets for nightclub doors and collected a lifetime of stories in the process.

items.title: Wendy Woke
items.description: An uncompromising writer who sees power structures behind every polished image and regards Vale Meridian glamour with ideological suspicion.

items.title: Cassette Carl
items.description: Streetwise and resourceful, Carl moves in circles where secrets have market value and information is currency.

items.title: Lady Helena de Brissac
items.description: Charismatic, pious and influential, Helena is used to commanding attention and trust while noticing the details others miss.

items.title: Wanda Wires
items.description: Quiet, practical and observant, Wanda works under Leo Lights and prefers equipment to celebrity egos.

items.title: Marshall 'Macho' Monroe
items.description: Patient, imposing and more sensitive about his acting than his size suggests, Marshall knows how to hold a room.

items.title: An old British passport
items.content: Found under a loose cushion beside the sofa: Patricia Margaret Thatcher, issued 1974, expired 1984. Nikki shows it; Tina ‘Tank’ Thatcher explains the name.
items.description: An expired pre-1988 British passport opened at the particulars page: Patricia Margaret Thatcher, born Sheffield 1946, profession 'civil servant', issued 1974 at Northallerton, expired 1984. Every number and office is invented and the image is watermarked for game use. Give it to Nikki with her Round 2 card; she shows it to Tina, who explains that Patricia Thatcher was her working name in intelligence. Crease it once so it does not look freshly printed.

items.title: Champagne service
items.content: Vance Vellum · ordinary champagne service, separate from Vale’s private wine
items.description: A waiter pouring champagne at the bar, with ice buckets and rows of glasses. This is Vance's Round 2 point in picture form: the general service was quite separate from Vale's private decanter.

items.title: A dance
items.content: Vance Vellum · reception
items.description: A couple dancing in the main room. The 'dance' among Vance's reception frames.

items.title: The decanter photograph
items.content: Vance Vellum · 10 October 1986, 19:29:10 · a woman from behind, her hand near the stopper. The frame does not show anything entering the wine.
items.description: Vance's decanter frame, the single most useful picture in the game. A woman seen from behind at the private drinks table, her hand on the stopper, a filled glass beside her; her face is completely hidden and nothing is shown entering the wine, so it places somebody there without naming them. Black and white on purpose. What can be recognised is long blonde hair, a dark draped gown with a line of pearls along the shoulder, and a wide pearl cuff on the reaching wrist: enough for Nikki and Dakota to stand by their Round 3 identifications, not enough to settle it alone. The figure's hair, gown and bracelet are what the witnesses recognise, so keep them consistent with the murderer's costume, which should include a wide cuff bracelet on the right wrist. Nine copies print, so Vance can leave one at every table and keep his own. Released in Round 2 inside the pack, never on its own; Nikki and Dakota recognise the woman in Round 3.

items.title: Greetings at the door
items.content: Vance Vellum · reception
items.description: Two women greeting each other at the door as a man watches from behind. One of the ordinary reception scenes Vance lists: people socialising, nothing about a recording or the decanter.

items.title: A group conversation
items.content: Vance Vellum · reception
items.description: Five guests raising champagne together: the 'group conversation' in Vance's list of reception frames.

items.title: Signing in the lobby
items.content: Vance Vellum · written on the print: 10·10·86  7:28 pm  V.V.
items.description: A young star in a pale cream suit signing an autograph in the lobby, head bent right down over the book so his face is not visible. The hidden face is deliberate: this is the only print whose subject is also a suspect, so the picture corroborates without doing the witness's job. Johnny's card is what names Robbie and places him there from 19:28 until the alarm. The time written on the border in Vance's hand also shows that he dates his frames, which matters when the decanter picture is questioned. The fan is a dark-haired woman in her fifties in red, chosen deliberately: an earlier version gave her long blonde hair and a dark dress, which inside the same pack read as the decanter woman one minute earlier and would have handed Veronica a false alibi.

items.title: Lucien Luxe beside the mirror
items.content: Vance Vellum · written on the print: 10·10·86  7:05 pm  V.V.
items.description: Lucien Luxe beside the gilt mirror: navy velvet frock coat, ruffled shirt, purple scarf and one black leather glove, which is exactly the brief Lucien was given, with the room reflected behind. The time on the border is 7:05 pm, well inside the reception and long before the toast. This is a portrait rather than evidence: Vance's own to hand to Lucien, and the glove is costume, not a clue. It takes the place of the old anonymous 'Beside the mirror' frame, whose woman seen from behind in dark velvet resembled the decanter woman closely enough to start a false identification.

items.title: A quiet word
items.content: Vance Vellum · reception
items.description: A man leaning in to speak to a woman holding a glass of red wine. Useful colour for the sleeve; it is not the private decanter and should not be presented as it.

items.title: Two guests
items.content: Vance Vellum · reception
items.description: Two women laughing with champagne under the chandelier. Filler for the sleeve, so the dropped-prints moment with Nikki has something to drop.

items.title: Vincent Vale at the microphone
items.content: For the public conclusion. Keep out of sight until Round 4.
items.description: Vincent Vale in black tie at the lectern microphone, a glass of his private red wine in his hand, mid-speech: Vance's Polaroid of tonight's toast and the last photograph of Vale alive. Shot from inside the crowd at guest height, so the foreground is backs of heads and no guest in the room is identifiable — the picture cannot be mined for who was standing where. It shows Vincent Vale as the room's host. For the GM to show during the credits, step 8 of the closing sequence. Keep it out of sight until then: it shows the private wine in his hand. It referenced CLUE_GM_R4 and CLUE_VV_EPILOGUE until those cards were retired into the closing-sequence document.

Everything that goes **inside** a clue envelope with its card, in the order the envelopes print (table, then character). Tick each box as the envelope is sealed.

items.title: GM running order
items.content:
# Vale Meridian — current GM running order

Host-only instructions; contains spoilers.

Facilitates the evening, hands out clues and a small number of evidence items, explains the procedure, helps introductions and manages practical staging. Guests discover and discuss the evidence. Gives the public conclusion in Round 4 after the tables have written their conclusions; does not supply investigative testimony during earlier rounds. Not a suspect.

Before guests arrive, sort ordinary cards, shared exhibits and private performance cards by the release sequence below. Give a short welcome explaining that guests play their characters, use the facts on released cards and talk to the named people or follow other interesting leads. Personal notes are optional. Fictional times and sightlines describe the story; guests need not reproduce them in the venue.

The characters Sheila Sparks and Felix Fortune are retired: their cards are inactive and nobody is sent to them, so the card counts below already leave them out.

Round 0 is mingling before seating and before the murder. The current arrival cards do not disclose who will die or when. Keep Vincent’s and Spinny’s necessary stage directions private: Vincent’s single private card goes to him at arrival; Spinny’s toast card is given immediately before the cue.

Beverly’s pre-party briefing already mentions a prepared but unserved dish. Her Round 0 card now states plainly that the sedative dish was meant for Vale; her later cards build to her admission. The Vincent performer becomes Peter without a real 25-minute wait: his first Peter card supplies the new role and late-arrival account. The performer’s pre-party briefing mostly describes Vincent, so do not assume they have read the longer Peter biography in the database.

## Round 0, step 1

Arrival: issue the 51 ordinary Round 0 cards while guests mingle, before seating or the murder. Each card names a small group of three or four: tell guests only “Your card names a small group; go and find them.” No meeting points or marshalling. Give Scooter the empty sealed compact and Spinny E1. Give the Vincent performer his single private card, CLUE_VV_R0, which covers the welcome, Marianne’s playful reading of his future, the toast and the collapse. Ordinary guests are not told who will die or when.

## Round 0, step 2

Privately give Spinny CLUE_SPINNY_TOAST_01 immediately before the staged toast; Vincent already has his card. Keep the house lights on. Veronica puts the compact on the private drinks table beside the decanter while the music covers the room; after the collapse, take it from the table discreetly and remove the seal.

## Round 1, step 1

After the staged collapse, release all 52 Round 1 cards. The Vincent performer changes to Peter and enters at fictional 19:55 without a real 25-minute delay; his first card introduces the new role. Give Peter the taxi note and Dakota the recovered unsealed compact.

## Round 2, step 1

Release all 52 ordinary Round 2 cards together. Hand Vance his nine photograph packs now, one for every table and one for himself, and let him take them round. GM uses CLUE_R2_VALE_01 privately and gives Dakota E2. Dakota has the compact; Scooter will ask her about it and borrow it to show Beverly. Allow conversations; no organised collection meeting.

## Round 3, step 1

Release all 52 ordinary Round 3 cards and the eight copies of the laboratory report CLUE_VV_R2 are in Donna’s Round 3 envelope (Item F); she hands one to every table. The photograph packs are already out from Round 2; Vance’s Round 3 card is where he explains the time on the decanter frame. Existing envelopes remain available. Guests pursue and share their own discoveries.

## Round 4, one sequence

Round 4 is no longer six cards handed out at six moments. Two documents replace them. Hand the closing-sequence sheet to yourself, Spinny and Donna at the start of the round: it carries every spoken line, all four music cues, the standing elimination, the arrest and the credits, in order. Their copies say [THE NAME]; yours has it filled in. The only other paper is Veronica's speech, handed over at step 6 — offer to read it for her, because she has never seen it and does not know until you name her a moment earlier. Everything else follows the sheet, so nothing else needs to be found mid-round.

## Practical evidence handling

Use an empty compact, dummy payments and ordinary stage glassware. The sealed compact goes to Scooter for Veronica, then Veronica sets it beside the decanter during the toast music, and the GM retrieves it from the table and removes the seal for Dakota’s post-collapse recovery. In Round 2 Scooter asks Dakota about it and borrows it to show Beverly. Do not ask Veronica to enact the fictional transfer or put anything into real food or drink. Fictional sampling is already represented by the report; no clothing swab or actual medical test is needed.

Keep Spinny’s envelope available from arrival; Dakota receives her matching envelope physically in Round 2, representing earlier fictional receipt. In Round 3 the owners can compare and show them without a compulsory trip to Donna. Donna hands the laboratory report to every table at the start of Round 3; her card also still sends people to her about it. Vance’s photographs all come out together in Round 2. Nine pictures print nine times each: hand Vance the nine packs at the start of Round 2, one for every table and one for himself, and let him take them round. Hold them until then — his Round 0 and Round 1 cards say he will not show a print until he has checked the time written on every one. The decanter frame is one picture inside the pack and is never handed over separately: it matches the murderer’s costume, so on its own it would identify Veronica by costume rather than by detection. Each table has to find it among the other eight, and Vance explains the time on it in Round 3. Nikki receives the printed passport with her Round 2 card and shows it to Tina; no search under cushions is needed. The toast portrait of Vincent Vale is for the public conclusion in Round 4, so keep it out of sight until then.

## Question notes (cross-table conversations)

Every Round 1–3 card that sends a guest to someone at another table has a pre-printed question note: 59 in all: 8 in Round 1, 26 in Round 2 and 25 in Round 3. The card's footer shows the note's key (for example "Note Q2-06"); the note shows the same key, who it is to and from, with tables, a short draft question in the asker's voice, two lines to add or change it, and a blank Reply section. Hand each guest their notes with that round's cards (they print in key order, table by table). The guest adjusts the draft if they like and sends it to the named table; the reply comes back on the same slip. Guests can still get up and talk instead. Same-table conversations and Round 0 have no notes. Twelve blank private notes remain for anything else.

## Conversations and closing

Help people locate the named person if needed. A short introduction is enough. Do not gather seven contacts, assign listeners, carry required messages or make Donna certify delivery. Let the room talk, then move to the closing round after reasonable discussion time. Do not invite final questions of named witnesses: with fifty-four guests that alone could run for hours, and the evidence has already been in the room for three rounds. The first public evidence explanation by the GM is the retained conclusion, given once the tables have discussed and each guest has written their own answer. Nobody votes and no slips are collected. Keep Veronica’s monologue, Donna’s arrest and the epilogue withheld until their individual cues.

Nobody has to perform the confession: offer to narrate it. The staged arrest involves no physical restraint. Follow the retained music cues and return promptly to the party.

## Whereabouts and testimony limits

Cassie and Beverly corroborate one another at the hatch; no service supervisor delivers new testimony. Larry’s two passes leave a gap before he stays beside Rex. Spinny continuously sees Ricky at the doorway; Johnny continuously sees Robbie in the lobby. The taxi-driver note supports Peter’s journey, not the appointment or clause. Frankie and Lola are mutual witnesses. Do not strengthen these accounts with invented staff calls or statements.

## Preparation status

The evidence objects are specified in physical-props.md. Make and check them in good time. A brief rehearsal should check card sorting, the compact’s practical handling, Peter’s transition and the closing music. This is practical preparation, not a receipt test for the guests.

# Vale Meridian — physical preparation checklist

Reviewed at publication. GM copy; contains story details.

Checked against the active clue records in the event database and the GM staging instructions in story/. Photographs and printed evidence are produced by Print Studio; pictures of people are placeholders until you add your own (docs/evidence-photos.md).

Preparation checklist only: nothing on it is bought, made or checked for you. Printed evidence and stationery are generated in Print Studio; the physical props, the decanter and the envelopes are yours to gather.

## Toast and event setup

### [ ] Distinctive private decanter with removable stopper — Required

Quantity: 1 · Responsible: GM / Vincent · Ready: Before arrival

Set on a small private drinks table or tray, visibly separate from general champagne service. The stopper matters to several witness accounts. Agree the location with Vincent, Dakota and Veronica (she must be able to reach it unseen).

Clue references: CLUE_VV_R0, CLUE047, CLUE_VV_R1, CLUE_R3_DAKOTA_01, CLUE_VVL_R3

### [ ] Red wine or a suitable red grape-juice substitute — Required

Quantity: Enough for the rehearsed pour and toast · Responsible: GM / Vincent · Ready: Before the toast

Use an ordinary drink agreed with the performer in the private decanter. The decanter and the red wine are real and Vale drinks from them during the toast. Serve the guests champagne, so that Vale is visibly the only person drinking red: that is what puts Lucien's Round 1 observation in front of the whole room rather than leaving it on a card. Nothing is added to the real drink.

Clue references: CLUE_VV_R0, CLUE_DONNA_R1, CLUE_VV_R2

### [ ] Vincent’s own drinking glass — Required

Quantity: 1, plus a practical spare · Responsible: GM / Vincent · Ready: Before the toast

Keep it with the private decanter and rehearse where it is put down for the staged collapse. Keep general champagne glassware separate from the decanter and its glass.

Clue references: CLUE_VV_R0, CLUE_DONNA_R1, CLUE_VV_R2

### [ ] Private drinks table or tray — Required

Quantity: 1 suitable venue surface · Responsible: GM / venue · Ready: Before arrival

A practical surface for the decanter and glass, with an agreed spot beside it for Dakota’s compact-recovery account. This is staging support for the named objects.

Clue references: CLUE_VV_R1, CLUE_VV_R0

### [ ] Music player, speakers, power and audio leads — Required

Quantity: 1 checked playback setup · Responsible: Spinny / GM · Ready: Before arrival

Prepare Died in Your Arms Tonight; It Had To Be You (Dark Version); Lux Aeterna; Killer Queen; Summer of ’69 or the agreed dance set. Use the retained cue cards. Comeback Girl never plays.

Clue references: CLUE_SPINNY_TOAST_01

### [ ] Stage/disco lighting and an operator’s cue — Required

Quantity: Use the venue’s agreed setup · Responsible: Leo / Wanda / Spinny · Ready: Before arrival

Rehearse the single twenty-second music-and-stage-light cue. Spinny leads: when his music rises Leo switches off some of the stage lights. House lights remain on. Check which stage lights Leo can switch off, who operates the controls and who gives the GM signal.

Clue references: CLUE_LEO_R0, CLUE_LL_R2, CLUE_WW_R1, CLUE_SPINNY_TOAST_01

### [ ] Working microphone and any spare batteries — Optional

Quantity: 1 if needed for audibility · Responsible: GM / venue · Ready: Before arrival

Useful for the welcome, toast and conclusion. The earlier broken microphone and two-second crackle are supplied recollections; no live fault or second distraction needs to be staged.

Clue references: CLUE046, CLUE053, CLUE099, CLUE_RR_R1

### [ ] Clock or timer and discreet cue sheet — Recommended

Quantity: 1 · Responsible: GM / Spinny · Ready: Before arrival

Time the actual twenty-second cue. Fictional 19:29, 19:30 and 19:55 do not require the venue clock to show those times. No special visible evidence clock needs constructing.

Clue references: CLUE_LL_R2, CLUE_VVL_R3, CLUE_VV_R0

### [ ] Vincent-to-Peter change and private holding space — Required

Quantity: 2 role badges; optional jacket/accessory change · Responsible: Vincent's player / GM · Ready: Ready before arrival; change in Round 1

Keep Peter’s badge out of the arrival pack. Agree a discreet exit, change and re-entry. The taxi note accompanies Peter; no real twenty-five-minute wait is needed.

Clue references: CLUE_VV_R0, CLUE170

## Evidence to prepare and handle

### [ ] Empty silver compact marked VV and removable seal — Required

Quantity: 1 compact, with a simple removable seal · Responsible: GM → Scooter → Veronica → private drinks table → GM → Dakota → Scooter · Ready: Round 0; reuse in Rounds 1 and 2

Deliver closed at arrival: Scooter hands it to Veronica in secret. During the toast music Veronica sets it unseen on the private drinks table beside the decanter. After the collapse the GM takes it from the table, removes the seal and gives it to Dakota. In Round 2 Scooter asks Dakota about it and borrows it to show Beverly. Keep it empty; C1 residue and the tests exist in the story/report.

Clue references: CLUE_SC_R0, CLUE_VER_R0, CLUE_VV_R1, CLUE_SC_R2, CLUE_VV_R2

### [ ] Two matching deep-red envelopes — Required

Quantity: 2, same paper, shade and size · Responsible: Spinny / Dakota · Ready: Spinny at arrival; Dakota in Round 2

Use matching stock and matching typing. Leave senders anonymous. The Round 2 issue represents Dakota’s earlier fictional receipt; both guests retain their envelopes for Round 3 comparison.

Clue references: CLUE_SPINNY_R0, CLUE037, CLUE149, CLUE144, CLUE_LL_R3

### [ ] Dummy payments for both envelopes — Required

Quantity: 2 small bundles of imitation money · Responsible: GM · Ready: Before arrival

Put a dummy payment in each deep-red envelope. Print the prop money from Print Studio (Evidence, "Prop money: Vale Meridian Glamour Pounds"): 24 notes, six to a landscape A4 sheet, cut along the marks and put 12 in each envelope. No real cash is needed.

Clue references: CLUE_SPINNY_R0, CLUE037, CLUE149

### [ ] Printed music and silence slips — Required

Quantity: 1 of each, from Evidence · Responsible: GM · Ready: Pack before arrival

Music: “At the toast cue, raise the music for twenty seconds. No delays.” Silence: “Say nothing about what you saw near the drinks.” Keep each inside its corresponding envelope.

Clue references: CLUE_SPINNY_R0, CLUE037, CLUE149

### [ ] Taxi-driver journey note — Required

Quantity: 1, from Evidence · Responsible: GM → Peter · Ready: Round 1

Passenger Peter Vale; collection outside the solicitor’s office, Cheltenham, 19:30; gala arrival 19:55; fictional date 10 October 1986. It supports the journey only, not the appointment or contract.

### [ ] Laboratory report, one per table — Required

Quantity: 8 copies of CLUE_VV_R2, one per table, in Donna's Round 3 envelope (Item F) · Responsible: GM → Donna → every table · Ready: Round 3, in Donna's envelope

Print the report eight times (Print Studio, Evidence) and put all eight in Donna's Round 3 envelope. Her card tells her to hand one to every table at the start of the round, so everybody can read the same findings. It includes the compact/wine connection, different dish sedative and limited fabric finding. No actual sample packets are required.

### [ ] Prepared decanter photograph — Required

Quantity: Part of Vance’s Round 2 pack, 9 copies · Responsible: GM → Vance · Ready: Round 2, inside the pack

Produced: print photo-decanter from Print Studio (Evidence). A woman from behind, her hand on the stopper, with the date and 19:29:10 in the caption; no powder transfer and no face. Black and white. The figure's recognisable features are long blonde hair, a dark draped gown with a pearl shoulder line, a wide cuff bracelet; keep them consistent with the murderer's costume, which should include a wide cuff bracelet on the right wrist.

Clue references: CLUE_VVL_R3, CLUE_NN_R3

### [ ] Passport in Tina’s former identity — Required

Quantity: 1 printed theatrical passport · Responsible: GM → Nikki → Tina · Ready: Hand to Nikki with her Round 2 clue (CLUE009)

Prepare a printed theatrical old passport with Tina’s character photograph and the name Patricia Margaret Thatcher. # Vale Meridian — Round 4: the closing sequence

**One script for the GM, DJ Spinny T and Inspector Donna Reed.** Everything Round 4 needs is on
this sheet. The only other piece of paper is the murderer's speech, handed over once, in the middle.

Set on the night of 10 October 1986

---

## How the name works

Wherever the murderer's name belongs, this script says **[THE NAME]**.

- **The GM** knows it, and the GM's copy has it written in.
- **Donna** does not need it in advance. The GM says it aloud seconds before her line, and she
  repeats it.
- **Spinny** never needs it at all.

So the three of you can rehearse this in full, beforehand, without two of you learning who did it.

**Hand this out at the start of Round 4.** One each. Keep the speech folded until step 6.

---

## The sequence

### 1 · The GM opens the closing round

**GM says:**

> "You have heard the witnesses. Talk it over at your table, then each write down who you think
> did it and the evidence that persuaded you."

**Spinny — cue 1.** On the words **"You have heard the witnesses"**, bring in
*It Had To Be You (Dark Version)* quietly. Well under the GM's voice. Texture, not foreground.

### 2 · Table discussion and written conclusions

Each table talks it over, and every guest writes their own conclusion on an accusation slip.
Nobody votes and nothing is collected or counted: the slips are each person's own answer, to
compare with the conclusion when it comes. This takes as long as it takes.

**Spinny — hold.** *It Had To Be You* plays all the way through underneath the talking. **Let it
run; do not restart it.** The discussion lasts as long as it lasts; the track is the bed under it,
not a timer.

### 3 · Pens down — the turn into the conclusion

**GM says:**

> "Pens down, please."

**Spinny — cue 2.** On **"Pens down"**, bring *It Had To Be You* to a close and **start**
*Lux Aeterna* **on loop**. Bring it up only as far as it can go while the GM stays comfortably
audible. It plays from here to the arrest, so set it looping and forget the running time: the
only thing that ends it is cue 3.

**GM — come in over the music.** *Lux Aeterna* runs for twenty seconds or so while the room
finishes writing and settles, then announce the elimination over it. Nothing is being held for
effect: the music starts, and you speak once it is up.

### 4 · The standing elimination

**GM:** runs the standing elimination from the tables. Everybody stands where they are sitting,
and people sit again as each test rules them out; nobody moves table. The GM's copy has the
words. Nobody is out of the game, and anyone who would rather stay seated may.

**Spinny — hold.** *Lux Aeterna* low. Everyone is at their own table, as on the table plan, and
stands and sits in place; nobody moves about the room. It stays quieter than it looks, so do not
lift the music to compete with it.

**Donna — join in.** Stand and sit with everyone else as the tests apply to you. Nothing else until step 7.

### 5 · The case, and the name

**GM:** sets out the case to those still standing. The GM's copy has it in full. Then:

> "The murderer is **[THE NAME]**."

### 6 · The speech

**GM:** hand over the speech and **offer to read it aloud instead**. Whoever receives it has never
seen it, has had no rehearsal, and does not know until this moment. At the slightest hesitation,
read it yourself and let them listen.

**Spinny — hold.** Keep *Lux Aeterna* low beneath it. Resist lifting it.

**Donna — stand by.** You are not waiting for a pause. When the speech ends the GM will say
**"Inspector, would you arrest them, and take them to the cells."** That sentence is your cue,
and Spinny's warning.

### 7 · The arrest ★

**GM:**

> "Inspector, would you arrest them, and take them to the cells."

**Donna — step forward.** Composed, unhurried, final.

> *Optional lead-in:* "This matter is concluded."
>
> **"[THE NAME], you are under arrest for the murder of Vincent Vale. You will come with me."**

**Spinny — cue 3.** On the words **"you are under arrest"** — **cut** *Lux Aeterna* dead and
**slam into Killer Queen at 0:29**, so it lands on **"She's a killer queen"**. Loud. Clean start,
no fade in, no intro. This is the release the whole evening has been holding back; let the room
react.

**Donna — the exit.** Invite them to walk out with you. **No physical restraint of any kind.** A
hand towards the door is enough. Let the applause happen.

**Donna — come back in.** Once you are both through the door, wait a moment, then walk back in together as *Killer Queen* fades. You are both in the credits, and both take a bow.

### 8 · The credits

**Spinny — fade.** After the first chorus of *Killer Queen*, bring it down. The credits run a little longer now: keep it low and steady.

**GM — read the credits.** Wait until Donna and the arrested guest are back in the room. Then unhurried, one name at a time, with applause between each.

**The first three bows — rehearsed.** The credits open with Donna, the arrested guest and Spinny. When your name is read, take a step forward, bow, and hold it for the applause. Everyone named after you will copy what you do, so make it clear and unhurried.

> "Ladies and gentlemen — Vale Meridian.
>
> We hope you enjoyed our little game, and got to know each other a little better along the way.
> A big thank you to everyone who played their part so well.
>
> The detective who closed the case: **Inspector Donna Reed**, *played by* **[player's name].**
>
> The person at the heart of it: **[THE NAME].**
>
> The man who set the mood all evening and cut the music at exactly the right moment:
> **DJ Spinny T**, *played by* **[player's name].**
>
> *[The GM reads the rest of the credits, a name at a time, from the GM's copy.]*
>
> And every one of you — the stars, the schemers, and the ones with something to hide.
> Please all stand up and take a bow.
>
> Thank you for taking part in our murder mystery, and I hope you enjoy the rest of the evening.
> Now over to the real star — **[your DJ’s name]**."

### 9 · Back to the party

**Spinny — cue 4.** On **"over to the real star — [your DJ’s name]"**, bring in *Summer of '69*, or
the agreed dance set. That line is the handover: the mystery is finished and the party is yours.

---

## Spinny's cue card

Four moves. Every one is triggered by a spoken word, not by a nod — including the last.

| # | Trigger | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "You have heard the witnesses" | *It Had To Be You (Dark Version)* in, quiet |
| — | discussion and written conclusions | **let it play through — never restart it** |
| 2 | "Pens down" | end *It Had To Be You* · **start** *Lux Aeterna* **on loop**, low |
| — | elimination, case and speech | **hold low — speech must stay audible** |
| 3 | "**you are under arrest**" | **cut** *Lux Aeterna* · **slam** *Killer Queen* **from 0:29**, loud |
| 4 | "over to the real star — [your DJ’s name]" | *Summer of '69* / dance set |

The only hard cut in the sequence is cue 3. Everything else is a fade. Your one-line warning that
it is coming is the GM saying "Inspector, would you arrest them, and take them to the cells."

**Your bow.** In the credits you are named third, straight after the arrested guest. Stand up at the desk and bow; the music stays low.

---

## Donna's cue card

| Beat | What you do |
|---|---|
| Elimination | Stand and sit with everyone else as the tests apply to you. |
| The case | Stay where you are. Do not move. |
| The speech | Stay where you are. Your cue is "Inspector, would you arrest them…" |
| Arrest | Step forward. Optional: "This matter is concluded." Then the line. |
| Exit | Invite them to walk with you. **No restraint.** |
| Return | Walk back in together as *Killer Queen* fades. |
| Credits | Named first: step forward and bow. Then bring the arrested guest forward for theirs — they have not rehearsed it, so you lead. |
| Final bow | Stand with everyone else. |

---

## What to rehearse

Worth practising:

- **The first three bows.** Donna bows, then brings the arrested guest forward; Spinny stands and bows at the desk. The rest of the room copies whatever these three do. Rehearse Donna's with a stand-in, since the real guest will not know until the night.

- **Cue 3.** The cut on "you are under arrest" is the one beat that has to land exactly. Run it
  until Spinny is cutting *on* the word rather than after it.
- **The handover.** "Inspector, would you arrest them…" → Donna's line → the cut. Three lines in a
  row from three people. Run them together a few times.
- **Cue 3 landing on the words.** *Killer Queen* starts at 0:29 so the first thing the room hears
  is "She's a killer queen". Check the start point against the file you will actually play:
  pressings and remasters differ by a second or two, and a second late loses the line.
- **The *Lux Aeterna* level.** It loops under the elimination, the case and the speech, so the
  length looks after itself; the level does not. Too loud and the case is lost, too quiet and the
  arrest has nothing to cut away from.

Not worth rehearsing:

- The discussion and the writing. Unpredictable length by design.
- The name. Donna hears it from the GM seconds before she needs it.

---

## On the night

- All three of you get this sheet at the start of Round 4.
- The speech is the only other paper, handed over once, at step 6.
- Nothing new is introduced once the pens are down. If a guest produces fresh evidence, it is too late and
  the GM will say so.

# Veronica Vane

Read this slowly. Short lines. Take a breath at each gap.

You have not seen this before and nobody expects you to have prepared. If you would rather not
read it aloud, hand it straight back and it will be read for you.

---

"Vince made control sound like a favour. A part. An introduction. A chance to begin again.

I was eighteen when I signed. Half of everything I have earned since has been his.

Tonight was meant to be mine. He was going to stand up and make it his.

*(pause)*

I asked Beverly for the sample. I told her Vince wanted to look at it. Scooter brought it to me,
sealed.

During the music, I went to his decanter. Nobody was watching. It took seconds.

*(pause)*

Beverly's dish never reached him. That one was hers. This one was mine.

I thought that if his hold on me ended, I would have my life back.

Instead I have brought all of us here."

preparation.title: Distinctive private decanter with removable stopper
preparation.detail: Set on a small private drinks table or tray, visibly separate from general champagne service. The stopper matters to several witness accounts. Agree the location with Vincent, Dakota and Veronica (she must be able to reach it unseen).

preparation.title: Red wine or a suitable red grape-juice substitute
preparation.quantity: Enough for the rehearsed pour and toast
preparation.detail: Use an ordinary drink agreed with the performer in the private decanter. The decanter and the red wine are real and Vale drinks from them during the toast. Serve the guests champagne, so that Vale is visibly the only person drinking red: that is what puts Lucien's Round 1 observation in front of the whole room rather than leaving it on a card. Nothing is added to the real drink.

preparation.title: Vincent’s own drinking glass
preparation.detail: Keep it with the private decanter and rehearse where it is put down for the staged collapse. Keep general champagne glassware separate from the decanter and its glass.

preparation.title: Private drinks table or tray
preparation.detail: A practical surface for the decanter and glass, with an agreed spot beside it for Dakota’s compact-recovery account. This is staging support for the named objects.

preparation.title: Music player, speakers, power and audio leads
preparation.detail: Prepare Died in Your Arms Tonight; It Had To Be You (Dark Version); Lux Aeterna; Killer Queen; Summer of ’69 or the agreed dance set. Use the retained cue cards. Comeback Girl never plays.

preparation.title: Stage/disco lighting and an operator’s cue
preparation.detail: Rehearse the single twenty-second music-and-stage-light cue. Spinny leads: when his music rises Leo switches off some of the stage lights. House lights remain on. Check which stage lights Leo can switch off, who operates the controls and who gives the GM signal.

preparation.title: Working microphone and any spare batteries
preparation.detail: Useful for the welcome, toast and conclusion. The earlier broken microphone and two-second crackle are supplied recollections; no live fault or second distraction needs to be staged.

preparation.title: Clock or timer and discreet cue sheet
preparation.detail: Time the actual twenty-second cue. Fictional 19:29, 19:30 and 19:55 do not require the venue clock to show those times. No special visible evidence clock needs constructing.

preparation.title: Vincent-to-Peter change and private holding space
preparation.when: Ready before arrival; change in Round 1
preparation.detail: Keep Peter’s badge out of the arrival pack. Agree a discreet exit, change and re-entry. The taxi note accompanies Peter; no real twenty-five-minute wait is needed.

preparation.title: Empty silver compact marked VV and removable seal
preparation.quantity: 1 compact, with a simple removable seal
preparation.owner: GM → Scooter → Veronica → private drinks table → GM → Dakota → Scooter
preparation.detail: Deliver closed at arrival: Scooter hands it to Veronica in secret. During the toast music Veronica sets it unseen on the private drinks table beside the decanter. After the collapse the GM takes it from the table, removes the seal and gives it to Dakota. In Round 2 Scooter asks Dakota about it and borrows it to show Beverly. Keep it empty; C1 residue and the tests exist in the story/report.

preparation.title: Two matching deep-red envelopes
preparation.when: Spinny at arrival; Dakota in Round 2
preparation.detail: Use matching stock and matching typing. Leave senders anonymous. The Round 2 issue represents Dakota’s earlier fictional receipt; both guests retain their envelopes for Round 3 comparison.

preparation.title: Dummy payments for both envelopes
preparation.detail: Put a dummy payment in each deep-red envelope. Print the prop money from Print Studio (Evidence, "Prop money: Vale Meridian Glamour Pounds"): 24 notes, six to a landscape A4 sheet, cut along the marks and put 12 in each envelope. No real cash is needed.

preparation.title: Printed music and silence slips
preparation.detail: Music: “At the toast cue, raise the music for twenty seconds. No delays.” Silence: “Say nothing about what you saw near the drinks.” Keep each inside its corresponding envelope.

preparation.title: Taxi-driver journey note
preparation.detail: Passenger Peter Vale; collection outside the solicitor’s office, Cheltenham, 19:30; gala arrival 19:55; fictional date 10 October 1986. It supports the journey only, not the appointment or contract.

preparation.title: Laboratory report, one per table
preparation.quantity: 8 copies of CLUE_VV_R2, one per table, in Donna's Round 3 envelope (Item F)
preparation.detail: Print the report eight times (Print Studio, Evidence) and put all eight in Donna's Round 3 envelope. Her card tells her to hand one to every table at the start of the round, so everybody can read the same findings. It includes the compact/wine connection, different dish sedative and limited fabric finding. No actual sample packets are required.

preparation.title: Prepared decanter photograph
preparation.quantity: Part of Vance’s Round 2 pack, 9 copies
preparation.detail: Produced: print photo-decanter from Print Studio (Evidence). A woman from behind, her hand on the stopper, with the date and 19:29:10 in the caption; no powder transfer and no face. Black and white. The figure's recognisable features are long blonde hair, a dark draped gown with a pearl shoulder line, a wide cuff bracelet; keep them consistent with the murderer's costume, which should include a wide cuff bracelet on the right wrist.

preparation.title: Passport in Tina’s former identity
preparation.when: Hand to Nikki with her Round 2 clue (CLUE009)
preparation.detail: Prepare a printed theatrical old passport with Tina’s character photograph and the name Patricia Margaret Thatcher. Pack it with Nikki Neon’s Round 2 clue (CLUE009) and hand both to her at the start of Round 2. Nikki shows it to Tina and asks her to explain the name. The discovery under the sofa cushion is supplied in the clue; no planted document or search under venue cushions is needed.

preparation.title: Vance’s Polaroid camera
preparation.detail: His arrival card says he circulates with a Polaroid. A non-working period camera is enough for the role. Film is optional for party snapshots; the Round 3 evidence image is prepared separately or described.

preparation.title: Sabrina’s notebook and pen
preparation.detail: Her arrival card explicitly says Vale told her to bring a notebook. Useful character dressing as well as somewhere to make personal notes.

preparation.title: Polly’s claim folder
preparation.quantity: 1 folder or clipboard with a few blank claim forms
preparation.detail: A retired insurance assessor's prop, for the look only. Use blank forms; nothing in it is evidence. Her cards give everything she knows.

preparation.title: Beverly’s medical-style bag
preparation.detail: Her Round 1 card mentions her medical bag. An empty bag supports the character; drugs, medical equipment and real sample containers are unnecessary.

preparation.title: Ronnie Reels’ camera or camcorder
preparation.detail: Supports his filming role and east-wall camera position. No recording of a real poisoning or reconstructing the fictional sightline is required.

preparation.title: Veronica’s recognisable gown or evening outfit
preparation.detail: The gown is named in sightings and the fabric account. Use the guest’s chosen outfit; the pale hem trace and F1 swab are described on cards and the report. No real powder, marking or swabbing of clothing is required.

preparation.title: Coats, wrap and Vance’s photograph packs
preparation.detail: Print all nine photographs from Print Studio (Evidence) nine times and make up nine identical packs, one per table and one for Vance: greetings, a dance, a group conversation, champagne service, the lobby signing marked 7:28 pm, Lucien beside the mirror marked 7:05 pm, two further reception views, and the decanter frame. Hand them out at the start of Round 2, not before. A plain envelope for each pack keeps the dropped-prints moment with Nikki usable. The coats and wrap still support the pocket and cloakroom accounts; no live pocket insertion or search under cushions is needed.

preparation.title: Wellness/cosmetics display bottle
preparation.detail: A cosmetic accessory for the described product business. Keep it empty and separate from evidence; the cards supply ingredient and supplier information.

preparation.title: Penny’s notebook and pencil
preparation.quantity: 1 small notebook and pencil, if desired
preparation.detail: An ordinary notebook and pencil can suggest Penny’s script-editing work. No prepared speech, script pages, hidden writing or additional evidence needs to be made.

preparation.title: Clue and private performer/GM cards
preparation.detail: 51 arrival cards, then 52 in each of Rounds 1–3. Keep the toast and closing instructions private until their cues. The laboratory report is counted separately above.

preparation.title: Name badges, holders and seating stationery
preparation.quantity: 55 badges; 54 holders; 54 place cards; 8 table signs
preparation.detail: Badges are 90 × 56 mm with crop marks, eight per A4 sheet. One performer swaps Vincent for Peter, so two badges are printed for that seat but 54 holders suffice; Peter’s badge prints on its own private sheet. Use holders or clips that fit the finished badge size. Counts come from the approved seating plan.

preparation.title: Clue envelopes and their labels
preparation.quantity: 207 envelopes; 207 labels on 12 Avery J8161 sheets
preparation.detail: Every character gets their own envelope for each round: 51 in Round 0 and 52 in each of Rounds 1 to 3. Print the labels from Print Studio (Voting & notes) on Avery J8161 or L7161, 63.5 × 46.6 mm, eighteen per sheet. Each round starts a fresh sheet, so the sorting stays honest and the part-used sheet at the end of a round leaves spare labels for anything written by hand. Each label carries the guest name to read across a table, the character underneath to confirm the right card, and the table number. Envelopes need to take a 186 × 130 mm card, so C5 or a similar size.

preparation.title: Voting slips and pens
preparation.quantity: 56 slips; about 1 pen per attendee plus spares
preparation.detail: Tables use the slips while they discuss who committed the murder: one accused name, with the motive, means and opportunity. Nobody collects them. Pen quantities are a practical host suggestion.

preparation.title: Private note sheets and spare plain paper
preparation.detail: The print app supplies To, From and a lined Message area, two A5 notes per landscape A4 sheet. Writing a note remains optional; guests can speak directly.

preparation.title: GM references, round dividers and packing supplies
preparation.quantity: The GM reference sheets; 8 release dividers; labelled folders/envelopes
preparation.detail: Keep the running order, this checklist, the envelope inclusions list and the guest lookup to hand. Use scissors or a trimmer, cream A4 paper/card and spare seals for preparation. Packing envelopes are distinct from the two deep-red evidence envelopes.

preparation.detail: These are earlier incidents at about 19:20–19:21. Do not break real items to recreate them. Optional dummy costume instruments add atmosphere only.

preparation.title: Ignition cable, guardrail and rehearsal inspection
preparation.detail: The isolated cable, stage positions and old inspection form establish accounts. No pyrotechnics, working ignition device, extra barrier or forged inspection sheet needs preparing.

preparation.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
preparation.title: Recordings, tapes, archive computer and Comeback Girl
preparation.detail: No working archive, CG-1 audio, transcripts or performance film needs making. Comeback Girl is never played. Ordinary party music remains required above.

preparation.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
preparation.title: Contracts, financial records and other paperwork
preparation.detail: No contract bundle, will, loan papers, supplier records, conviction file, guest-list leak, publicity note, poem or signature specimen is required. Guests use their supplied knowledge; the taxi note and lab report are the specific printed documents listed above.

preparation.section: Story references: no physical preparation required
preparation.title: Chemical samples, medicines, fabric swab and herbs
preparation.detail: The compact stays empty. No stimulant, sedative, costume powder, C1/W1/D1/F1 sample pots or real testing is needed.

preparation.title: Handcuffs, restraint and an epilogue jacket note
preparation.detail: The arrest is a spoken invitation to accompany Donna, with no restraint required. The retained epilogue explicitly needs no extra prop.
